blogs.title: Why AI Might Stop Using Tokens: The Big Idea Behind Byte Latent Transformer
blogs.description: An accessible introduction to BLT that explains what tokenization is, why it has been a hidden bottleneck in large language models, and how BLT replaces fixed tokens with raw bytes and flexible patches. The post would focus on the paper's core claim: byte-level models can now match token-based models at scale.

blogs.title: From Bytes to Patches: How BLT Decides Where to Spend Compute
blogs.description: A deep but reader-friendly explainer on BLT's most novel idea: dynamically grouping bytes into patches based on prediction difficulty. It would break down entropy patching with intuitive examples, showing why easy text can be processed in larger chunks while harder text gets more attention.

blogs.title: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens: The Efficiency Story in Plain English
blogs.description: A performance-focused post that explains the paper's scaling results without heavy math. It would cover how BLT can reduce inference cost by up to roughly 50%, why larger patches can free up compute for a bigger model, and what 'fixed inference budget' means for real-world AI deployment.

blogs.title: Why Byte-Level AI Is More Robust to Typos, Weird Spelling, and Low-Resource Languages
blogs.description: A practical look at BLT's robustness benefits. The post would highlight the paper's findings on noisy text, spelling and character-level tasks, phonology, and translation for lower-resource languages, showing why working directly with bytes helps models handle the messy long tail of human language.

blogs.title: Inside the BLT Architecture: The Three-Part Design That Makes Byte-Level LLMs Work
blogs.description: A system-design oriented post that explains BLT's local encoder, global latent transformer, and local decoder in simple terms. It would show how the model mixes small byte-level modules with a large patch-level model, helping readers understand why BLT is not just 'a transformer on bytes' but a new architecture built for efficiency.

blogs.title: Can We Turn Today's LLMs Into Tokenizer-Free Models?
blogs.description: A forward-looking article based on the paper's experiments initializing BLT from Llama 3. It would explore the idea of 'byte-ifying' existing models, why that could reduce retraining costs, and what this might mean for the future of adapting foundation models without being locked into a tokenizer.
